open.finding: .sdlc/transcript-turn-accuracy/01-prd.md:22 (AC2) — AC2 says only TRANSFER_FAILED forces a zero-turn call to count as failed, but the code also emits TRANSFER_TIMEOUT (session.py:345, calls.py:389 groups both), so a timed-out flow-only Dial could be built as a success; fix: extend AC2 to cover TRANSFER_TIMEOUT.

.sdlc/transcript-turn-accuracy/01-prd.md:37 (AC15) — AC15 adds a call-to-answering-agent link but no criterion requires that agent to share the call's tenant_id, so per-agent counts could include another tenant's call (lesson 48); fix: add a same-tenant criterion, enforced when the link is written and in the count query.

.sdlc/transcript-turn-accuracy/02-design.md Risks (disposition-drift bullet) — The tripwire expects 4 Hangup reasons in callflow/runner.py, but runner.py has only 3 distinct ones (flow_budget, flow_complete, retries_exhausted); transfer_refused is emitted at callflow/handler.py:117 and goes through the same Hangup branch at handler.py:132, so the assertion fails on correct code. Fix: scan both runner.py and handler.py and assert the exact set of 4.

services/conversation/pipeline.py:1309 — The transfer-refused apology nested in _run_turn is iterated with a plain async for and not wrapped in aclosing. On a hang-up, its GeneratorExit write runs only from the asyncgen finalizer, which can run after end_call pops _sessions, so the [transfer_failed] row is silently dropped. This is not a regression, but it is the same class as carried item 2.

services/conversation/pipeline.py:1133 — Merge risk, not a defect: fix/tts-failure-handling changes _spoken_reply (CJK _join_sentences) and the max-duration record_turn near line 1046, which this diff also edits, so expect a conflict. Interrupted replies also join spoken pieces with a trailing space, which leaves spaces between CJK sentences.
uncovered — pipeline.py:1309 transfer-refused apology iterated without aclosing; GC-finalizer ordering not driven through servicer

services/conversation/servicer.py:587 — AC7 is met only at the level of what was sent, not what was played: the servicer has no pacing and the gateway buffers audio, so sentences synthesized ahead of playback are recorded as spoken even when a barge-in during sentence one means the caller never heard them; a multi-chunk sentence also counts in full once its first chunk is sent, and test_servicer_spoken_record.py holds synthesis back, so it cannot see this; state the limit in the PR body.

services/conversation/pipeline.py:1309 — Carried and still open: the transfer-refused apology inside _run_turn is iterated with a plain async for and not aclosing, so on a hang-up its GeneratorExit branch runs from the finalizer after end_call, where the new session_id-in-_sessions guard silently drops the [transfer_failed] row; no test drives this path.

services/conversation/pipeline.py:1133 — Carried and still open: spoken pieces are stored as piece plus a trailing space and joined, so CJK replies keep spaces between sentences; this overlaps the _join_sentences change on fix/tts-failure-handling.

services/conversation/session.py:70 — Merge risk, not a defect: fix/tts-failure-handling adds end_call_without_audio next to the new on_sent field and rewrites the tts_payloads/audio_sent condition right above the servicer.py:587 on_sent call, so expect textual conflicts and keep on_sent after the cancel drain when resolving them.
